semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {تُرْجَعُ الأمور}: It has already been mentioned in al-Baqara that the two Kufan "brothers" (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the jīm, in the active voice, while the rest read it in the passive voice, throughout the Quran. The Shaykh said here: "The majority read «تُرْجَعُ» in the passive; al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿraj read it in the active." This is strange of him, and the same sort of thing has happened to him before, as I pointed out.
And His saying: {يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ}: its like has already been discussed in Sūrat Saba.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {وَمَا لَكُمْ لاَ تُؤْمِنُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., what has settled upon you [so that you are] not believing?
And His saying: {والرسول يَدْعُوكُمْ}: a circumstantial clause from «يُؤمِنون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So they are two nested ḥāls, and «لِتُؤْمنوا» is attached to «يَدْعو», i.e., he calls you to faith, as you say, 'I called him to such-and-such.' It is also possible that the lām is for cause, i.e., he calls you to Paradise and to Allah's forgiveness for the sake of faith. But there is some remoteness in this."
His saying: {وَقَدْ أَخَذَ}: also a ḥāl. The majority read «أَخَذَ» in the active voice, the agent being Allah the Exalted, because He was mentioned earlier. Abū ʿAmr read «أُخِذ» in the passive, the agent being omitted because it is known. «ميثاقَكم» is accusative in the majority's reading and nominative in Abū ʿAmr's reading. As for «إنْ كنتم», its apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then what prevents you from faith?" It is also said that the implied form is: "if you are believers for any reason that necessitates it, then this is that which necessitates it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied: "if you are believers, then you hold an honourable rank." The two readings of «يُنَزَّل», lightened and doubled (the zāy with shadda), have already been discussed in al-Baqara. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أَنْزَل» as a past-tense verb.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {أَلاَّ تُنفِقُواْ}: like His saying {وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاَّ نُقَاتِلَ} [al-Baqara: 246]. The original is "fī an lā tunfiqū" (in [not] spending); when the preposition was omitted, the well-known disagreement arose [about the status of «أنْ» and what it governs]. Abū al-Ḥasan holds that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), as its explanation has already been given in al-Baqara.
His saying: {وَللَّهِ مِيرَاثُ}: a circumstantial clause from the agent of "settling" (istiqrār) and its object, i.e., what prevents you from spending in the way of Allah, when the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him? This is a state that contradicts your miserliness.
His saying: {لاَ يَسْتَوِي مِنكُم مَّنْ أَنفَق}: There are two views on the agent of «يَسْتوي». The more apparent is that it is «مَنْ أَنْفَق». On this view an omitted conjoined element (maʿṭūf) is necessary to complete the sentence. Al-Zamakhsharī implied: "Among you, those who spent before the conquest of Mecca and the strength of Islam are not equal to those who spent after the conquest; he omitted it because the indication is clear." Abū al-Baqāʾ implied "and those who did not spend", saying: "What indicates the omitted element is His saying {مَّنْ أَنفَقَ مِن قَبْلِ الفتح}." The first is better, because the context brings the verse only to distinguish between those who spent at two different times.
The second view: its agent is a pronoun returning to spending (infāq), i.e., the kind of spending is not equal, since some of it took place before the conquest and some after it, and these two types differ. On this view «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ, «أَعظَمُ» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «مَنْ». This ought not to be permitted at all; it is as though this i'rab-writer overlooked His saying «منكم». Had this speaker parsed «منكم» as a fronted khabar and «مَنْ» as a postponed mubtadaʾ, with the implied meaning "among you are those who spent before the conquest, and among you are those who did not spend before it and did not fight", and this omitted because the speech indicates it, it would have been sound; but he overlooked the word «منكم».
His saying: {وَكُلاًّ وَعَدَ الله الحسنى}: The majority read it accusative, as a fronted object, and it is written in their codices «وكلاً» with an alif. Ibn ʿĀmir read it nominative, and there are two views on this. The more apparent is that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the following clause as its khabar and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e., "Allah promised him." Similar is:
4231 - Umm al-Khiyār has begun to claim ... against me a sin, all of which I have not committed
with «كلُّه» nominative, i.e., "I did not commit it." The Basrans permit this only in poetry, like the saying:
4232 - And Khālid, whom our chiefs praise ... in truth, is not praised for falsehood
Ibn Mālik reported a consensus of the Basrans and Kufans that this is permitted if the mubtadaʾ is «كلاً» or something resembling it in need of completion and in generality; I have not seen this from anyone else. Something similar has already been discussed in Sūrat al-Māʾida at His saying {أَفَحُكْمَ الجاهلية يَبْغُونَ} [al-Māʾida: 50]. The saying "kullu-hu lam aṣnaʿ" has been transmitted only with the nominative, though it would be possible to put it in the accusative, saying "kulla-hu lam aṣnaʿi" as a fronted object. The people of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) said: because he intended the generality of negation, not the negation of generality, for the former is more eloquent. They counted among this the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him:
"Kull dhālika lam yakun" (None of that came to be). Had he said "lam yakun kullu dhālika", it would have been a negation of generality, whereas the intention is generality of negation.
The second view: «كل» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and {وَعَدَ الله الحسنى} is an adjective (ṣifa) of what precedes, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e., "and those are each one whom Allah has promised the best reward." If it is said: omission is present here too, and you have returned to what you fled from, the answer is: omitting the returning pronoun from an adjective is frequent, unlike omitting it from a khabar. An example of omitting it from an adjective is the saying:
4233 - I do not know whether distance has changed them ... or the length of time, or wealth they acquired
i.e., "they acquired it", and the like is plentiful. In the codices of Syria it is written «وكلٌّ» without an alif, so Ibn ʿĀmir's reading agrees with his codex. «الحُسْنى» is a second object, and the first is omitted in the nominative reading; as for the accusative reading, the first object is fronted before its operator.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {مَّن ذَا الذي يُقْرِضُ}: This and what follows have already been treated fully, praise be to Allah, together with the differences among the readers about it, in Sūrat al-Baqara. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: "The nominative is by conjunction or by cutting off and resumption." ʿĀṣim read «فيضاعِفَه» in the accusative, with the fāʾ [of the answer] to a question. There is some unease in that. Abū ʿAlī said: "Because the question did not fall on the loan, but on the one who gives the loan; the fāʾ puts in the accusative only a verb that is a response to a verb asked about; but this group carried it according to the meaning, as though His saying {مَّن ذَا الذي يُقْرِض} were equivalent to His saying 'Does anyone lend to Allah?'" End of quotation. What Abū ʿAlī said is not accepted: do you not see that the accusative occurs after the fāʾ in answer to a question with nouns, even when no verb has preceded, as in "Where is your house, that I may visit you?" and likewise "Who calls me, that I may answer him?", "When will you travel, that I may accompany you?" and "How are you, that I may keep company with you?" For the question is about the person calling, about the adverb of time and about the state, not about the verb. Ibn Kaysān reported from the Arabs: "Where did Zayd go, that we may follow him?" and "Who is your father, that we may honour him?"

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَرَى}: There are several views on it. First: it is governed by the "settling" (istiqrār) that operates in «لهم أجرٌ», i.e., a reward has settled for them on that day. Second: it is governed by an implied verb, i.e., "remember", so it would be an object. Third: [the implied sense is] "they are rewarded on the day you see", so it is an adverbial in its original sense. Fourth: its operator is «يَسْعى», i.e., the light of the believing men and women runs on the day you see them; this is its basic form. Fifth: its operator is «فيضاعفَه». Abū al-Baqāʾ stated the last two.
His saying: {يسعى}: a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual (physical sight). This holds if he does not make it operate on «يوم». «بين أيديهم» is an adverbial of the running, and it may be a ḥāl from «نورُهم».
His saying: {وَبِأَيْمَانِهِم}, i.e., and in the direction of their right sides. This is the majority's reading, I mean with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of yamīn. It is also said that the bāʾ means «عن» (from), i.e., from all their directions; He singled out the right sides only because they are the noblest of directions. Abū Ḥaywa and Sahl ibn Shuʿayb read it with kasra [«بإيمانهم», "by their faith"]. This verbal noun is conjoined to the adverbial before it.
The bāʾ is causal, i.e., it runs, being thus and thus, because of their faith. Abū al-Baqāʾ said its implied form is: "they deserved it by their faith", or "by their faith it will be said to them: your glad tidings."
His saying: {بُشْرَاكُمُ}: a mubtadaʾ, with «اليومَ» an adverbial and «جناتٌ» its khabar, with an omitted muḍāf (governing noun), i.e., "entering gardens". This clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of an implied saying, which is also the operator of the adverbial, as mentioned above. Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative of «جنات» as a ḥāl, with «اليومَ» as the khabar of «بُشْراكم»." He said: "That «جنات» is a ḥāl has no meaning, as there is no sense of a verb in it. He also permitted «بُشْراكم» to be in the position of the accusative, [meaning] 'they give them glad tidings with the glad tidings', with «جنات» put in the accusative by «البُشرى». All of it is remote, because one may not separate the ṣila (relative clause) and the relative noun by «اليوم»." End of quotation. It is strange of al-Farrāʾ that something unintelligible, and impermissible by the craft [of grammar], should issue from him: how could «جنات» be a ḥāl, and who would be the owner of the ḥāl?

semin-durr:13-13.t:
And His saying: {يَوْمَ يَقُولُ}: a badal (substitute) for «يومَ ترى», or governed by «اذْكُر» (remember). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears to me that its operator is {ذلك هُوَ الفوز العظيم}, and the meaning of 'triumph' becomes more majestic, as though He were saying: the believers triumph through mercy on the day when the hypocrites are overtaken by such-and-such, because a person's appearing on the day his enemy and opponent is obscure is more wondrous and majestic." The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of his words and his implication is that «يومَ» is governed by 'triumph' (al-fawz). This is not permitted, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has been described before taking its complements, so it may not operate. Had its adjective been made to operate, it would be permitted, i.e., 'that whose worth is great on the day'." I say: What Ibn ʿAṭiyya said was stated explicitly by Makkī, who said: "«يومَ» is an adverbial whose operator is that triumph, or it is a badal from the first «اليوم»."
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 12]: accusative as a ḥāl, whose operator is the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is: "your glad tidings is your entering gardens, abiding therein." The agent was omitted, being the pronoun of the one addressed, and the maṣdar was added to its object, becoming "entering of gardens"; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi took its place in i'rab. It is not permissible for «بُشْراكم» to be its operator, because it is a maṣdar that has been predicated about before its complements are mentioned, so separation by a foreign element would follow. The apparent sense of Makkī's words is that it is an operator on the ḥāl, for he said: "«خالدين» is accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm." The operator on a ḥāl is the operator on its owner, so «بُشْراكم» would have to be the operator, and in that lies the separation between the maṣdar and what it governs already mentioned.
His saying: {لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}: the lām is for conveying. As for «انْظُرونا»: the majority read «انظرونا» as an imperative from naẓar (looking). Ḥamza read «أَنْظِرونا» with a cut-hamza and kasra on the ẓāʾ, from inẓār in the sense of waiting, i.e., wait for us so that we may catch up with you and take light from your light. The first reading may also have this meaning, since one says "naẓarahu" meaning "he waited for him". That is because the sincere ones are hurried to Paradise on swift mounts, and the hypocrites say: wait for us, for we are on foot and cannot catch up with you. It may also be from naẓar meaning seeing, because when they look at them they face them, and the place is lit for them; this is more fitting to His saying {نَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُّورِكُمْ}. Al-Zamakhsharī stated this sense. But the Shaykh said: naẓar in the sense of seeing does not take a direct object except in poetry; it takes its object only through «إلى». [Translator's note: the source text repeats the clause "it does not take a direct object except in poetry, it takes ... only through..." twice, apparently a copyist's duplication; translated once.]
His saying: {وَرَآءَكُمْ}: two views. The more apparent is that it is accusative through «ارْجِعوا» in the sense: return to the standing-place, to where we were given this light, and seek it there from whom we may take light; or return to the world and seek light by acquiring its cause, which is faith; or return disappointed and stand aside from us and seek another light, for you have no way to this light. The second: «وراءكم» is a noun of verb (ism fiʿl) containing a pronoun as agent, i.e., "go back, go back"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and he forbade it being an adverbial of «ارْجِعوا», saying: because of its little benefit, since returning is only ever to the rear. This is invalid, because the benefit is considerable, as its explanation has already been given.
His saying: {فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُم بِسُورٍ}: The majority read it passive. The deputy agent may be «بسورٍ», which is the apparent view, or the adverbial. Makkī said: "The bāʾ is redundant, i.e., 'a wall was struck'", then said: "the bāʾ is attached to the maṣdar, i.e., 'a striking with a wall'". This is contradictory, unless the copyists have distorted it for him and the original was "or the bāʾ is attached to the maṣdar", with the deputy agent being the adverbial. In sum, it is weak.
Al-sūr is the encircling structure. Its derivation was given at the beginning of al-Baqara.
His saying: {لَّهُ بَابٌ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the genitive, an adjective of «سُوْر».
His saying: {بَاطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرحمة}: this clause may be in the position of the genitive, as a second adjective of «سُوْر», and it may be in the position of the nominative, as an adjective of «بابٌ», which is preferable because of its nearness; the pronoun returns to the nearest unless there is an indication [otherwise].
Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «فَضَرَبَ» in the active voice, the agent being Allah or the angel.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {يُنَادُونَهُمْ}: it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بَيْنهم»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is weak because of a ḥāl coming from a muḍāf ilayhi outside the exceptional places. It may also be resumptive, which is the apparent view.
His saying: {أَلَمْ نَكُن}: it may be an explication of the calling, and it may be governed in the accusative by an implied saying.
His saying: {الغرور}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the ghayn, and it is an adjective on the pattern faʿūl, meaning Satan. Simāk ibn Ḥarb read «الغُرور» with ḍamma, which is a maṣdar; its like has already been discussed.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {فاليوم}: accusative through «يُؤْخَذُ». The negative «لا» is not considered [an obstacle], which is the view of the majority. It was mentioned at the beginning of this topic, at the end of al-Fātiḥa, that there are three views on it. Ibn ʿĀmir read «تُؤْخَذُ» in the feminine because of the word «فِدْية»; the rest read it with the masculine yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative and because of the separation.
His saying: {هِيَ مَوْلاَكُمْ}: it may be a maṣdar, i.e., "your guardianship", meaning the possessor of your guardianship; it may be a place, i.e., the place of your guardianship; and it may mean "more fitting for you" (awlā bikum), as you say "he is his mawlā". «وبئس المصيرُ» means: it [is the evil destination].

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {أَن تَخْشَعَ}: the agent of «يَأْنِ», i.e., has the humbling of their hearts not drawn near? Abū al-Baqāʾ said of the lām: "it is for clarification", so on this it is attached to an omitted element, i.e., "I mean those who", but there is no need for it. The majority read «أَلَمْ»; al-Ḥasan and Abū al-Sammāl read «ألَمَّا», and you already know the difference between the two particles from what has preceded. The majority also read «يَأْنِ», the imperfect of anā, i.e., the time has come and drawn near, like ramā, yarmī. Al-Ḥasan read «يَئِنْ», the imperfect of āna, also meaning "the time has come", like bāʿa, yabīʿu.
His saying: {وَمَا نَزَلَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read «نَزَل» lightened, in the active voice. The rest of the Seven likewise, except that it is doubled (shadda on the zāy). Al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «نُزِّلَ» doubled, in the passive. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «أَنْزَل» in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted. As for «ما» in «ما نَزَلَ» lightened, it must be a noun (ism), and it may not be a maṣdar particle, lest the verb be without an agent; in the others it may be a maṣdar particle or mean "that which". If you say: in the reading of al-Jaḥdarī and those with him it too ought to be a noun, so that the verb is not without a nominative, the answer is that the preposition phrase, His saying «من الحق», takes the place of the agent.
The majority read the third person in «ولا يَكونوا», following what has preceded. Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with the tāʾ of the second person, as a shift of address (iltifāt). This may be accusative, conjoined to «تَخْشَعَ» as in the third-person reading, and it may be a prohibition, so that «لا» is prohibitive and the verb is jussive by it. It may also be a prohibition in the third-person reading, which would be a transition to forbidding those believers from being like those before them, as in "let not Zayd stand".
His saying: {الأمد}: the majority read the dāl lightened, in the sense of "end/limit", as you say "amad of so-and-so", i.e., his limit. Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read it with the dāl doubled, meaning a long time. [Translator's note: the source says "بمعنى العامَّة" ("meaning the general public") where "end/limit" (الغاية) is evidently intended, as the example "his ghāya" shows; translated according to the example.]

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {المصدقين والمصدقات}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr lightened the ṣād in both; the rest of the Seven doubled it. Ibn Kathīr's reading is from taṣdīq (believing as true), i.e., they believed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he brought, as in the saying of the Exalted {والذي جَآءَ بالصدق وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ} [al-Zumar: 33]. The reading of the rest is from ṣadaqa (charity), which suits His saying «وأَقْرَضوا». The original is al-mutaṣaddiqīn wa-l-mutaṣaddiqāt, then it was assimilated; Ubayy read it so. The first may be preferred on the ground that lending makes mention of charity unnecessary.
His saying {وَأَقْرَضُواْ}: three views. First: it is conjoined to the active participle in «المُصَّدِّقين», because when it occurs as the ṣila of «al-» it takes the place of the verb, as though it were said "those who gave charity and lent"; this is the view of most i'rab-writers, and al-Fārisī, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ held it. It is invalid because it requires separation between the parts of the ṣila by a foreign element: do you not see that «المُصَّدِّقات» is conjoined to «المصَّدِّقين» before the ṣila is complete? And it may not be conjoined to «المُصَّدِّقات» because the pronouns differ in masculine and feminine.
Second: it is parenthetical between the noun of «إنَّ» and its khabar, which is «يُضاعَفُ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is said only so that the past tense not be conjoined to an active participle." I do not know what this obstacle is, because whenever an active participle is the ṣila of «al-» it suits the three times; had he objected by what I mentioned, the separation by a foreign element, he would have been right, but that was hidden from him as it was hidden from those greater than he, al-Fārisī and al-Zamakhsharī.
Third: it is the ṣila of an omitted relative noun, which the first indicates, as though it were said "and those who lent", like the saying:
4234 - Is he who satirizes the Messenger of Allah among you ... and he who praises him and helps him, equal?
i.e., "and he who helps him"; the Shaykh preferred this, and you already know what is in it from the beginning of this work.
His saying {يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمْ}: two views on the deputy agent. One, the apparent one, is that it is the preposition phrase after it. The second is that it is the pronoun of taṣdīq, which requires an omitted muḍāf, i.e., "the reward of taṣdīq".

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُوا}: [a mubtadaʾ], and «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ; «هم» may be a third mubtadaʾ with «الصِّدِّيقون» its khabar, and it with its khabar is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. «هم» may also be a separator (faṣl), so «أولئك» and its khabar form the khabar of the first.
His saying {والشهدآء}: two views are possible. It is conjoined to what precedes, and the stop at «الشهداء» is complete; He reports of those who believed that they are truthful ones and witnesses. If it is said: the martyrs are distinguished by other attributes beyond that, like the seven mentioned, the answer is: their being singled out for mention is because of their superiority over others, not for restriction.
The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and there are two views on its khabar. One is the adverbial after it. The second is His saying «لهم أَجْرهُم», either the clause or the preposition phrase alone, with the nominative as its agent. The place of stopping is not hidden given the i'rab I mentioned.
Al-ṣiddīq is a form of intensiveness, and generally comes only from a triliteral. Some said: "misskīk" has come from amsaka. This is a mistake, because one says masaka as a triliteral, so «misskīk» is from that.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ}: The majority read «تَفاخُرٌ» with tanwīn, described by the adverbial or governing it; al-Sulamī made it a muḍāf to it.
His saying: {كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ}: it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لَعِبٌ», because it has the sense of description; and it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "that is like the likeness of". Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that it be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of what precedes. Makkī did not specify it, saying: "an adjective of «تَفاخُر»". There is something to consider in that, because of his singling it out from among what precedes. He also allowed it to be a khabar after a khabar for «الحياة الدنيا».
«مُصْفارَّاً» has been read, from iṣfārra, which is more intensive than iṣfarra.
His saying: {وَفِي الآخرة}: a fronted khabar, and what follows is a mubtadaʾ. He reports that in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Him and good pleasure. This is a fine meaning, namely that He set against the punishment two things, forgiveness and good pleasure, so it is of the type «لن يَغْلِبَ عُسْرٌ يُسْرَين» ("One hardship will never overcome two eases").

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {عَرْضُهَا كَعَرْضِ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. The clause is an adjective of «جنة», and likewise «أُعِدَّتْ». It may also be that «أُعِدَّتْ» is resumptive.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ}: the agent of «أصاب». «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) because the two conditions are met [a negative context and an indefinite noun]. He made its verb masculine because the feminine is figurative.
His saying {فِي الأرض}: it may be attached to «أصاب», it may be attached to «مصيبةٍ» itself, and it may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «مصيبة»; on this it is suitable to judge its position as genitive, looking at the form of what it describes, and as nominative, looking at its position, since it is an agent. «المُصيبة» (calamity) is mostly used for evil. It is also said that what is meant is all events, good and evil; on the first view it is asked: why was it mentioned and not the good? The answer: He singled it out for mention because it is more important to humankind.
His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ}: a ḥāl from «مصيبة»; this is permitted although it is indefinite because it is specified, either by operation or by description, i.e., "except as written".
His saying {مِّن قَبْلِ}: an adjective of «كتاب», and it may be attached to it, as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, because here it is a noun for what is written and is not a maṣdar. The pronoun in «نَبْرَأَها» apparently returns to the calamity. It is also said: to the selves; it is also said: to the earth, or to all of that; al-Mahdawī said it, and it is fine.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {لِّكَيْلاَ}: this lām is attached to His saying «ما أصابَ», i.e., We informed you of that so that there not befall you despairing grief or exalting joy; as for less than that, a person is not held to account for it. Here «كي» governs the accusative by itself, so it is only a maṣdar particle, because the genitive lām has entered upon it. Abū ʿAmr read «بما أتاكم» shortened, from itiyān (coming), i.e., what came to you. The rest of the Seven read «آتاكم» lengthened, from ītāʾ (giving), i.e., what Allah gave you. ʿAbd Allāh read «أُوْتيتم».

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {الذين يَبْخَلُونَ}: the like of this was already given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, and I spoke on it sufficiently, so there is no point in repeating it.
His saying {فَإِنَّ الله هُوَ الغني}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «فإن الله الغنيُّ» omitting «هو», which is absent in the codices of Medina and Syria. The rest include it, and it is present in their codices, so each agrees with his codex. Abū ʿAlī said: "Whoever includes «هو», it is fitting that it be a separator (faṣl) and not fitting that it be a mubtadaʾ, because a mubtadaʾ may not be omitted." He means that its being a separator is made preferable by its omission in the other reading, since if it were a mubtadaʾ its omission would be weak, especially when what follows it can be the khabar of what precedes. Do you not see that if you said "inna Zaydan huwa al-qāʾimu", omitting «huwa» would not be good, since «al-qāʾimu» is fit to be the khabar of «inna»? This is like what they said of the ṣila: the returning pronoun that is a nominative by inchoation is omitted under conditions, among them that what follows it not be fit to be the ṣila, as in "jāʾa alladhī huwa fī al-dār" or "huwa qāʾimun abūhu", for lack of indication. But an opponent may dispute Abū ʿAlī and say: "I do not commit myself to building one of the two readings on the other; how many pairs of readings differ in meaning, like the two readings of {والله أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 36] and «وضَعَتْ» [Translator's note: the source prints the same form twice here; the second is presumably «وَضَعْتُ»]; yet agreement of two readings in one meaning is preferable." This is not disputed.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ}: a circumstantial clause from «الحديد».
His saying: {مَّعَهُمُ}: an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e., "becoming with them". We need this only because the messengers were not sent down, whereas the sense of the speech requires that they accompany the Book in descending. As for al-Zamakhsharī, he interpreted the messengers as the angels who bring revelation to the prophets, so the accompaniment is realized.
His saying: {وَلِيَعْلَمَ}: conjoined to His saying «ليقومَ الناسُ», i.e., "We sent Our messengers and did such-and-such so that people may establish [justice] and so that Allah may know". The Shaykh said: "It is a cause for sending down the Book, the Balance and the iron." The first is more apparent, because the helping of Allah and His messengers suits the sending.
His saying {وَرُسُلَهُ}: conjoined to the object of «يَنْصُرُه», i.e., "and helps His messengers". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may not be conjoined to «مَنْ», so as not to separate by it the preposition «بالغَيْب» from what it is attached to, «يَنْصُرُ»." I say: His making the reason what he mentioned, the separation between the preposition and what it is attached to, suggests that the meaning would otherwise be sound but for this obstacle. That is not so, since the implied form would become: "so that Allah may know whoever helps Him unseen, and so that He may know His messengers", and this is a meaning that is not at all sound, so there is no need to mention that. «بالغيب» is a ḥāl, and its like was given at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {فَمِنْهُمْ مُّهْتَدٍ}: the pronoun may return to «الذُّرِّيَّة» (the offspring), which is preferable because it was mentioned earlier in the wording. It is also said that it returns to those to whom [messengers] were sent, as «أَرْسَلْنا» and «المرسلين» indicate them.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {الإنجيل}: It was already mentioned at the beginning of Āl ʿImrān that al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa on the hamza. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its matter is lighter than that of «birṭīl» and «sikkīn» for those who transmit them with fatḥa on the first letter, because the word is non-Arabic and need not preserve Arabic patterns." Abū al-Fatḥ said: "It is a pattern with no parallel."
His saying: {وَرَهْبَانِيَّةً ابتدعوها}: there are two views on its accusative. One: it is conjoined to «رأْفَةً ورحمةً». «جَعَلَ» is either in the sense of "created" or in the sense of "made", and «ابْتدعوها» on this is an adjective of «رَهْبانية». The mention of innovation was specific to it because compassion and mercy in the heart are matters of innate disposition in which a person has no acquisition, unlike monasticism, which consists of bodily acts in which a person has acquisition. But Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade this view, because what Allah made, they do not innovate. The answer is what preceded: since it is acquired, this is sound for it. He also said: "It is also said that it is conjoined to it, and «ابتدعوها» is an adjective of it. The meaning is: He made obligatory upon them the observance of a monasticism they innovated; therefore He said: {مَا كَتَبْنَاهَا عَلَيْهِمْ إِلاَّ ابتغآء رِضْوَانِ الله}."
The second view: it is accusative through an implied verb explained by the overt one, the case being one of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun). Al-Fārisī, al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and a group inclined to this, except that it is said to be the i'rab of the Muʿtazila; for they say: whatever is a human act is created by him; so since mercy and compassion are Allah's act, He attributed their creation to Himself, while monasticism, not being Allah's act but the servant's, which he performs independently, He attributed its innovation to him. There is another place, more fitting than this one, for refuting them, and I will explain it, God willing, in «al-Aḥkām».
The Shaykh rejected this i'rab on technical grounds: it is required of the noun on which the verb is preoccupied that it be fit for nominative by inchoation, and «رهبانيةً» is indefinite with nothing to license inchoation, so its accusative is not fit as ishtighāl. There is something to consider in this, for we do not first concede the condition, and the reading of the one who read «سورةً أنزَلْناها» in the accusative as ishtighāl indicates it, as I set out in its place. Even if we concede it, there is a licensing factor here, namely conjunction. Of that is the saying:
4235 - I have patience, and complaint before my killer ... so is there anything more wondrous than this that a man has heard?
and the saying:
4236 - He dined while a star had shone; and when ... your face appeared, its light hid every rising [star]
Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik mentioned that. Al-Ḥasan read «رَآفة» on the pattern faʿāla. «الرَّهْبانيةُ» is a relative adjective (nisba) from «الرَهْبان», which is faʿlān from rahiba, as they say «al-khashyān» from khashiya. The sense of this root was fully discussed in al-Māʾida. It has also been read with ḍamma on the rāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though it were a nisba to «الرُّهْبان», the plural of rāhib, like rākib and rukbān."
The Shaykh said: "It is preferable that it be a nisba to rahbān, I mean with fatḥa, and it was altered, because nisba is a domain of alteration; had it been a nisba to the plural ruhbān, it would be returned to its singular, unless it had become like a proper name, in which case it is attributed to it, like «al-anṣār»."
His saying: {مَا كَتَبْنَاهَا}: an adjective of «رَهْبانيةً», and it may be a resumptive report of that.
His saying: {إِلاَّ ابتغآء رِضْوَانِ الله}: several views. First: it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from what is an object of purpose. The meaning: We did not decree it upon them for any reason except the seeking of Allah's good pleasure, «كتب» meaning "decreed", so it becomes "We decreed it upon them in seeking Allah's good pleasure"; this is Mujāhid's view. Second: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī said this and mentioned no other, i.e., "but they innovated it". Qatāda and a group went this way; they said its meaning is: He did not make it obligatory upon them, but they innovated it. Third: it is a badal from the accusative pronoun in «كَتَبْنَاها»; Makkī said this and it is problematic: how can it be a badal when it is neither the first, nor part of it, nor comprised by it? It may be said that it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because pure monasticism observed with due observance may include in it the seeking of Allah's good pleasure, and it becomes like your saying "al-jāriya mā aḥbabtuhā illā adabahā" (the girl: I loved her only for her manners), where «illā adabahā» is a badal of inclusion from the pronoun in «aḥbabtuhā»; this is the utmost of contrivance for making this view sound, and Allah knows best.
The nominative pronoun in «رَعَوْها» returns to those mentioned earlier. The meaning: not all of them persisted in observing it, although this was found in some of them. It is also said that it returns to the kings who fought them; and it is said, to their allies. «حَقَّ» is accusative as a maṣdar.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ}: this lām is attached to the meaning of the requestive sentence which contains the sense of a condition, since the implied form is: "if you fear Allah and believe in His messengers, He will give you such-and-such, so that [the People of the Book] not know". There are two views on this «لا». One, the well-known one among grammarians, exegetes and i'rab-writers, is that it is redundant (zāʾida), as in {مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12] and {أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ} [Yā Sīn: 31], with disagreement about these two verses. The implied form: Allah informed you of that so that the People of the Book know their lack of power over anything of Allah's bounty and the certainty that the bounty is in Allah's hand. This is clear and evident, and in it is only the addition of what has been established as an addition commonly and widely.
The second: it is not redundant, and the meaning is "so that the People of the Book not know the incapacity of the believers". Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted that, and these are his words; he had said before that: "«لا» is redundant and the meaning is: so that the People of the Book know their incapacity". This is not straight, because the believers too are incapable of anything of Allah's bounty. And how would this speaker deal with His saying {وَأَنَّ الفضل بِيَدِ الله}? It is conjoined to the object of the negated knowing, so the implied form would become: "so that the People of the Book not know that the bounty is in Allah's hand"; negating knowledge of this is not at all straight. Naturally it is a discarded view, which I mentioned to alert to its invalidity.
The majority's reading is «لئلا» with kasra on the lām of purpose (lām kay), followed by a lightened fatḥa-vowelled hamza. Warsh changes it into a pure yāʾ, which is a regular lightening, as in «miya» and «fiya» for «mi'a» and «fi'a». That it is redundant is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, al-Jaḥdarī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama «لِيَعْلَم», omitting it, and by the reading of Ḥaṭṭān ibn ʿAbd Allāh «لأَنْ يعلمَ», with «أَنْ» shown. Al-Jaḥdarī also, and al-Ḥasan, read «لِيَنَّعَلَمَ». Its origin is like the one before, «li-an ya'lama»; the hamza was changed to yāʾ because of its fatḥa after kasra, as already mentioned that this is regular, like Warsh's reading «لِيَلاَّ»; then the nūn was assimilated into the yāʾ. The Shaykh said: "Without ghunna, like Khalaf's reading of {أَن يَضْرِبَ} [al-Baqara: 26] without ghunna." End of quotation. So the pronunciation became «li-yanna'lama». As for his saying "without ghunna", absence of ghunna is not a condition for the soundness of this matter; it came about by coincidence, and had he assimilated with ghunna that would be permitted. Its omission in these readings supports its redundancy in the well-known reading.
Al-Ḥasan also read, in what Abū Bakr ibn Mujāhid transmitted from him, «لَيْلاً يَعْلَمَ», with fatḥa on the lām and a quiescent yāʾ, like the woman's name [Laylā], with the verb after it nominative. Its analysis: its origin is «li-an lā», the lām being the genitive lām but vowelled with fatḥa in a known dialect; they recited:
4237 - I want, so as to forget her mention ...
with fatḥa on the lām. The hamza was omitted arbitrarily, the nūn was assimilated into the lām, so three like letters were brought together and pronouncing it became heavy, so the middle one was changed to yāʾ for lightness, and the pronunciation became «laylā» as you see; and the verb is nominative because «أَنْ» is the lightened one, not the accusative-governing, and its noun, as established, is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the negation particle separates it from the verb that is its khabar.
Al-Ḥasan also read, in what Quṭrub transmitted from him, «لِيْلا» with kasra on the lām and quiescent yāʾ, and the verb nominative; it is like the previous in analysis, the most that can be said being that it came with a kasra on the lām as in the famous dialect. It was transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās «لكي يعلَمَ» and «كي يعلم», and from ʿAbd Allāh «لكيلا»; all of these contradict the great majority and the script of the codex.
The majority read {أَنْ لا يَقْدِرُون} with the nūn retained, «أَنْ» being the lightened one; ʿAbd Allāh [read it] with the nūn dropped, «أَنْ» being the accusative-governing one. This is very irregular, because the accusative-governing particle does not occur after knowing.
His saying: {يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ}: apparently resumptive. It is also said: it is a second khabar of «الفضل». It is also said: it is the only khabar, with the preceding preposition phrase a ḥāl, which is an inseparable ḥāl (ḥāl lāzima), because its being in Allah's hand the Exalted never changes.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {للَّهِ}: two views are possible regarding this lām. The first: it is redundant (zāʾida), like it in «نَصَحْتُ لزيدٍ» (I advised Zayd) and «شكرْتُ له» (I thanked him), since one says «سَبَّحْت الله تعالى» (I glorified Allah the Exalted); the Exalted said: {وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 206]. The second: it is for giving the reason (taʿlīl), i.e. it performed glorification for the sake of Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {لَهُ مُلْكُ}: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position.
His saying: {يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ}: three views are possible regarding this clause. The first: it has no grammatical position, like the one before it. The second: it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He has sovereignty". [Translator's note: so in the text («هو له مُلك»); the intended implied form is presumably «هو يُحيي ويُميت» (He gives life and causes death).] The third: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «له», so what governs it is the [verbal notion of] settledness (istiqrār). The two objects of giving life and causing death are not mentioned, since the purpose is to mention the two acts only.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {هُوَ الأول والآخر}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of the wāw? I say: the first wāw signifies that He combines the two attributes of firstness and lastness; the third, that He combines manifestness and hiddenness; and as for the middle one, that He combines the whole of the first two attributes and the whole of the other two."
